Just past puberty, Ibn Abbas passed before a praying row at Mina and none objected, and Mahmud recalled the Prophet throwing water from his mouth onto his face at five.
On a day set aside to teach women, the Prophet said a woman whose three or even two young children die will be shielded by them from the Fire.
An orphan stood with Anas behind the Prophet; young Ibn Abbas joined the rows and the Eid; Friday bathing binds those past puberty; Isha was delayed till children slept.
A Muslim whose three children, or even two, die before puberty is granted Paradise and screened from the Fire.
A sick Jewish boy serving the Prophet embraced Islam; Ibn Abbas was a child among the weak; every child is born with true faith and receives the funeral prayer.
A Muslim whose three children die before puberty enters Paradise; Ibrahim has a wet-nurse there; Allah knows what pagans' children would have done; every child is born with true faith.
When a man called 'Abul-Qasim' meaning someone else, the Prophet told people to name themselves with his name but not with his kunya.
Ibn Umar, refused for Uhud at fourteen, was allowed into the Trench battle at fifteen, the age a caliph called the limit of manhood; Friday bathing binds those reaching puberty.
The Prophet praises Um Khalid's yellow shirt in Ethiopian, lets her play with the seal of prophethood, and three times wishes her to wear it out, and she lived long.
People may name sons after the Prophet but not use his kunya, for he is Qasim, the distributor; he praises the Ansar for refusing that title to a boy's father.
People may name themselves after the Prophet but not use his kunya, as he said when a man in the market called out Abu-l-Qasim.
When a man said a black child had been born to him, the Prophet, likening it to a grey camel among red ones, said the colour may come from heredity.
The Prophet put chewed dates in newborns' mouths and blessed them, among them Asma's son Abdullah bin az-Zubair, and named Abu Musa's son Ibrahim and Abu Talha's son Abdullah.
The Prophet let little Um Khalid play with his Prophethood seal, called Hasan and Husain his flowers, carried Umamah in prayer and kissed Al-Hasan; well-treated daughters shield from Fire.
A child the Prophet gave Tahnik urinated on him, and he poured water over it; he held Usama and Al-Hasan on his thighs and prayed for mercy on them.
People may take the Prophet's name but not his kunya Abu-l-Qasim; a father was told to name his son Abdur-Rahman; the Prophet renamed Al-Mundhir and Zainab, but Hazn refused Sahl.
Take the Prophet's name but not his kunya, for he is Al-Qasim who distributes Allah's blessings; Satan cannot take his form in dreams, and he named Abu Musa's son Ibrahim.
The most awful name in Allah's sight on the Day of Resurrection is that of a man calling himself King of Kings, which some said means Shahan Shah.

The Prophet blessed children, stroking As-Sa'ib's head, pouring water on an infant's urine, spraying Mahmud's face, touching another's eye; men sought partnership with Abdullah bin Hisham, whom he blessed.
A Muslim who loses three children will not be touched by the Fire except as far as fulfils Allah's oath.
A bedouin whose wife bore a black child was asked about grey camels among his red ones and told the child had most probably inherited its colour from ancestors.
To a bedouin who doubted his black son was his, the Prophet pointed to grey camels among red ones, colour inherited from ancestors, and did not let him deny paternity.
